steps: Read the focused resources and do the starter exercise below; ask the named reviewer about a concrete blocker.
Create a minimal Express app serving EJS templates with ordinary HTML/CSS and small JavaScript. Pin Node/package versions and add an environment example without secrets.

Implement username/password registration with validation, unique username and a maintained password-hashing library. Use express-session with a SQLite-backed session store; regenerate the session on login and destroy it on POST logout. Do not write cryptography or email flows.

Use HttpOnly, SameSite cookies, CSRF tokens on state-changing forms, and a session secret outside source control. Document localhost HTTP cookie settings and HTTPS-only settings for any future hosting.
Protect home/upload/dataset/run/evaluation routes. Agree shared Account/session SQL with W3 and form field/error locals with W2; no separate frontend API is required.

With AI, use Node child_process.spawn with shell:false to send two synthetic records over stdin to AI’s toy Python script and receive one JSON response. AI owns the Python code; W1 owns the JavaScript adapter. This spike is a handoff check, not model training.
Check registration, duplicate username, weak/mismatched passwords, failed login, logout, CSRF rejection and logged-out routes. Confirm Node can report a failed Python command clearly.
Attach actual output and acceptance evidence; record actual hours and request review before Done.
accept: A teammate starts Express from the README; passwords are hashed with a maintained library and secrets are uncommitted.
